The 1938 National Bureau of Standards paper RP1142 records one concrete run that processed 240 gallons of dewaxed Oklahoma City crude at pressures down to 1 mm Hg, confirming that narrow, stable fractions could be taken without cracking.

claims.claim: The 1926 paper by B.T. Brooks in Industrial & Engineering Chemistry described atmospheric batch still conditions that produced cracked, unstable lubricant fractions.
claims.episode_span: The 1926 paper by B.T. Brooks in Industrial & Engineering Chemistry described how those conditions produced cracked, unstable fractions that needed extra treating steps later.
claims.source_title: The Distillation of Lubricating Oils under High Vacuum
claims.supporting_quote: this article discusses high-vacuum distillation techniques for lubricating oils, including operating conditions, equipment considerations, and advantages over atmospheric methods

claims.claim: The 1930 Bureau of Mines report BM-RI-2996 recorded vacuum distillation apparatus operating at pressures suitable for lubricant oils without cracking.
claims.episode_span: The 1930 Bureau of Mines report BM-RI-2996 and the 1931 patent US1804941 both record operating pressures between 50 and 100 mm Hg, which allowed distillation temperatures to remain under 425 °C.
